posts.title: Drawing a frame for a very tall rider
posts.excerpt: At 194 cm, Kenji had never ridden a bicycle that fitted. Haru on the fitting, the drawing and the three tubes he had to order specially.
posts.content:
Kenji came to the fitting with a folder of photographs: every bicycle he had owned since school, each one too small. At 194 cm with long legs and a short back, he had spent twenty years stretched over frames drawn for someone else.

Starting on the jig

The jig tells us more than a tape measure. We set the saddle height first, then moved the bars until his shoulders dropped and his hands went quiet. The numbers that came out were not extreme: they were simply not anything a factory makes.

A tall frame is not a normal frame made longer. Every tube has to be thought about again.

Haru Kiyose

Three special tubes

A long head tube, a top tube of 61 cm and a down tube with thicker walls, so the front end would not flex under him. We ordered them from our tube supplier in Osaka and waited two weeks.

The frame went home last Saturday. Kenji sent a photograph from the riverside the next morning, the first one in the folder where the bicycle looks the right size.

posts.title: Why we still lace wheels by hand
posts.excerpt: A machine can lace a wheel in four minutes. Mio takes an hour and a half. What happens in the extra eighty-six minutes.
posts.content:
Most wheels in the world are laced by machines and finished by a person in a few minutes. It works, mostly. But the spokes are rarely even in tension, and an uneven wheel goes out of true the first time it meets a pothole.

Four passes, two rests

Mio brings the tension up in four slow passes, checking each spoke by ear and with a gauge. Between passes she squeezes pairs of spokes together to settle them at the hub and the rim. Then the wheel rests overnight on the rack.

  • Even tension, within five percent spoke to spoke
  • True and round to a tenth of a millimetre
  • Stress-relieved twice, so it stays that way

It takes an hour and a half for a front wheel. We think that is the cheapest ninety minutes in a bicycle.

posts.title: Winter service: what we check first
posts.excerpt: Ren's list for the season of wet roads and short days: five things to look at before December, three of them free.
posts.content:
The first cold week always brings the same bicycles to the repair bench: chains gone orange, brake pads worn to the metal, lights that stopped working in August. Most of it can be caught early.

Five things, in order

  • Chain: clean it, oil it, and measure it for wear
  • Brake pads: look for the grooves; when they are gone, so is the grip
  • Tyres: cuts, glass and the depth of the tread
  • Lights: charge them and check the mounts
  • Cables: rust where they enter the housing

If you do the first three at home, bring it in for the rest. A safety check and tune is on the price list and usually done the same day.

posts.title: A dawn ride along the Sumida
posts.excerpt: Once a month we leave the workshop door at five in the morning and ride north along the river. Notes from September's ride.
posts.content:
We met at the workshop at a quarter to five, eleven of us, with coffee from the flask Ren brings every time. By five we were on the river path heading north, the city still asleep on both banks.

The mist sat on the water until Senju. Nobody talked much. That is the point of the dawn ride: an hour and a half of steady pedalling before the day starts, and breakfast together afterwards at the bench.

Join the next one

The ride is free and slow, and any bicycle in working order is welcome. The date goes out in the monthly letter.

posts.title: Leather saddles: the first month
posts.excerpt: A new leather saddle feels like a plank. A month later it feels like yours. How to get through the weeks in between.
posts.content:
Every leather saddle we sell comes with the same warning: the first week is not comfortable. Thick vegetable-tanned leather needs time and warmth to take the shape of the rider.

What helps

  • Ride it often, in short rides, rather than one long one
  • A thin coat of balm on the underside in the first week only
  • Keep it dry: use the cotton cover when you park in the rain
  • Leave the tension bolt alone for the first 500 km

By the end of the month it should feel firm but kind. If it still hurts, bring it in and we will look at the angle together.

posts.title: Choosing a bell nobody minds
posts.excerpt: A bell is the only part of a bicycle that talks to other people. Why we chose a small brass one with a long, soft ring.
posts.content:
On a shared path, the bell is how a bicycle says excuse me. Too loud and it startles; too thin and nobody hears it. We tried eleven bells before choosing the one we sell.

Solid brass rings longer and lower than steel or aluminium. One flick gives a note that carries forty metres without making anyone jump. Left unlacquered, it slowly darkens to the colour of old coins.

We fit it on the left of the bars, close to the grip, so a thumb finds it without looking.

products.name: Kuramae Road Frameset
products.short: Our everyday road frame: thin lugged chromoly tubes, a quiet grey finish and room for 32 mm tyres.
products.description:
Brazed at the bench in Kuramae from double-butted chromoly tubing, with hand-filed lugs and a fork crown cut to match. The geometry is calm rather than racy: a long wheelbase, a little more trail, and clearance for 32 mm tyres and full fenders.

Sold as a frameset (frame, fork and headset). Ask us about a fitting first: we keep stock sizes from 50 to 60 cm and draw a custom frame when none of them is right.

products.name: Handbuilt Front Wheel
products.short: A polished box-section rim laced three-cross to a sealed-bearing hub, tensioned and trued by hand.
products.description:
Mio laces every wheel at the truing stand by the window, brings the spokes up to even tension in four passes and stress-relieves them twice. It leaves the workshop true to a tenth of a millimetre and stays that way.

Free re-true within the first six months.

products.name: Silver Hub Wheelset
products.short: A matched pair laced to our silver high-flange hubs: the wheels we fit to most of our builds.
products.description:
Front and rear wheels laced to polished high-flange hubs with sealed cartridge bearings. Built in one sitting so the pair matches in tension and feel, then checked again after a week on the rack.

Rear hub available for 8 to 11 speed cassettes or single speed: tell us at checkout.

products.name: Touring Saddle, Leather
products.short: Thick vegetable-tanned leather over a steel frame, stitched by hand. Firm at first, yours after a month.
products.description:
Cut from a single piece of vegetable-tanned leather, stitched around the edge and set on a black steel frame with long rails. It starts firm and slowly takes the shape of the rider.

Comes with a small tin of leather balm and a cotton rain cover.

products.name: Waxed Canvas Bar Bag
products.short: A roll-top handlebar bag in charcoal waxed cotton, big enough for a jacket, a lunch and a book.
products.description:
Sewn for us in a small canvas workshop in Saitama from heavy waxed cotton with webbing straps and a stiffened back, so it holds its shape on the bars. The roll top keeps the rain out; two side pockets keep a phone and keys at hand.

Re-wax once a year and it will outlast the bicycle.

details.Mounting: Two bar straps, one head-tube strap

products.name: Brass Bell
products.short: A small, solid brass bell with a long, clear ring that carries without startling anyone.
products.description: Turned from solid brass and left unlacquered, so it slowly darkens to a soft gold. One flick gives a long, clear note: polite on the riverside path, loud enough in traffic.

products.name: Bike Fit Session
products.short: An hour and a half on our fitting jig with Haru, and a sheet of measurements to keep.
products.description:
We measure you, watch you pedal on the adjustable jig and set saddle height, reach and bar drop until the position feels easy. You leave with a printed sheet of numbers that fits any bicycle.

The fee is taken off a custom build if you order one within three months.
